# API Contracts Governance v1

This repository currently exposes a narrow contract and runtime foundation for `SWE_BODELNING`, plus runtime-enabled `profile_inputs`, `release_eval`, `profile_dossier`, `export_package`, JSON, Markdown, PDF, and DOCX export artifact, bundle/package manifest, and final bundle/archive artifact support for `"CMD_PROFILE"` only.

The canonical model-information, uncertainty, and fail-closed principles that govern how this repository structures information are defined in `docs/MODEL_INFORMATION_PRINCIPLES_v1.md`; they apply to both `SWE_BODELNING` and `"CMD_PROFILE"` and remain upstream of future substantive rule work.

The canonical runtime jurisdiction profile identifiers in this slice are `SWE_BODELNING` and, for `profile_inputs`, `release_eval`, `profile_dossier`, `export_package`, JSON, Markdown, PDF, and DOCX export artifact, bundle/package manifest, and final bundle/archive artifact, `"CMD_PROFILE"`.
The central jurisdiction/profile registry scaffold is defined in `packages/governance/src/jurisdiction-profile-registry.js`; it is machine-readable, contains the explicit supported `SWE_BODELNING` entry plus the explicit `"CMD_PROFILE"` entry, and centralizes supported-profile capability checks for governance, API, and internal projection dispatch without changing the current `SWE_BODELNING` surface shapes.
The canonical jurisdiction/profile registry schema surface is defined in `schemas/jurisdiction-profile-registry.json`, exported through `packages/schemas`, validates the current runtime registry shape, currently requires the supported `SWE_BODELNING` entry plus the explicit `"CMD_PROFILE"` entry, and allows later additional profile entries in the contract without introducing unsupported runtime behavior outside the enabled capabilities in this slice.
The next documented profile declaration is `"CMD_PROFILE"`. The provided raw required lane input list is `"cmd_primary_signal"`, `"cmd_primary_signal"`, `"cmd_primary_signal"`; because current schema conventions require a unique machine-readable required lane set, the canonical profile-input schema in `schemas/cmd-profile-input.json`, exported through `packages/schemas`, normalizes that required lane set to `"cmd_primary_signal"` only. Runtime support is enabled for `profile_inputs`, `release_eval`, `profile_dossier`, `export_package`, `export_package_json_artifact`, `export_package_markdown_artifact`, `export_package_pdf_artifact`, `export_package_docx_artifact`, `export_package_bundle_manifest`, and `export_package_bundle_archive_artifact` on `"CMD_PROFILE"`: the governance runtime registry now includes an explicit `"CMD_PROFILE"` entry with those capability flags set to `true` through the final bundle/archive surface in this slice.

The `SWE_BODELNING` profile input contract is defined in `schemas/swe-bodelning-profile-input.json`, exported through `packages/schemas`, and used by the thin profile input API surface.
The central governance profile-input adapter/dispatch scaffold is exported from `packages/governance/src/index.js`; it is keyed by `jurisdiction_profile_key`, contains the explicit supported `SWE_BODELNING` adapter entry plus the explicit `"CMD_PROFILE"` adapter entry, and selects canonical profile-input validation and derivation through that registry without changing the current `SWE_BODELNING` output shape.
The explicit `"CMD_PROFILE"` profile-input adapter entry is wired only to the documented `schemas/cmd-profile-input.json` validation/canonicalization seam for the normalized `"cmd_primary_signal"` lane set. Runtime support is enabled for `profile_inputs` in this slice: authenticated API and persistence boundaries now accept `"CMD_PROFILE"` profile inputs through the shared adapter/validation seam, while all export-related `"CMD_PROFILE"` capability gates remain fail-closed/unsupported.

### Profile Input Semantic-Fact Mapping Prerequisites

`profile_input` semantic-fact adoption is only partially implemented. The canonical
machine-readable presence-only alignment surface is defined in
`schemas/profile-input-semantic-fact-alignment.json`, exported through `packages/schemas`,
and is grounded in `docs/MODEL_INFORMATION_PRINCIPLES_v1.md` and
`schemas/semantic-fact-model.json`. This contract-only alignment is intentionally limited to
the one currently safe dimension, `presence_status`; implementing any broader
`profile_input` semantic-fact alignment would still require guessing beyond the current repo
contracts.

The current `profile_input` contracts for `SWE_BODELNING` and `"CMD_PROFILE"` are concrete
enough to freeze only these already-native signals for later semantic-fact work:

- profile identity and canonicalized lane-set signals:
  `jurisdiction_profile_key`
  `profile_input_lane_snapshot` required lane keys
  `profile_input_summary.required_lane_count`
  `profile_input_summary.missing_value_lane_keys`
- canonical lane entry structure:
  `profile_input_lane_snapshot.*.has_value`
  `profile_input_lane_snapshot.*.value`
  `profile_input_lane_snapshot.*.evidence_object_ids`
- canonical value-presence summary:
  `profile_input_summary.lanes_with_value_count`

Supported-to-map dimensions:

- `presence_status` only. The canonical `profile_input` semantic-fact alignment surface
  relates required-lane value presence already contract-defined in the current
  `profile_input` seam through the fixed lane sets, `has_value`,
  `profile_input_summary.required_lane_count`,
  `profile_input_summary.lanes_with_value_count`, and
  `profile_input_summary.missing_value_lane_keys`.
- The canonical presence-only alignment covers exactly these safe current cases for both
  `SWE_BODELNING` and `"CMD_PROFILE"`:
  required lane with value -> `{ "presence_status": "present" }`
  required lane already marked missing in the canonical `profile_input` snapshot/summary ->
  `{ "presence_status": "missing" }`
- Raw empty payload content is not independently normalized at the `profile_input` seam.
  Any broader empty-value inference remains outside this alignment surface unless and until
  the `profile_input` contracts explicitly define it.

The following neutral semantic-fact dimensions remain unassigned for `profile_input` and are
not yet contract-defined in this repository:

- `source_status`
- `verification_status`
- `dispute_status`
- `consistency_status`

Current `profile_input` contracts do not yet define profile-input-level source/support,
verification, dispute, or consistency semantics. In particular,
`profile_input_lane_snapshot.*.evidence_object_ids` remain opaque reference ids in this seam
and are not yet contractually sufficient to map `source_status` without guessing.

Freeze rule:

- no `profile_input` semantic-fact alignment should be implemented beyond the documented
  safe `presence_status` cases until the missing dimensions are explicitly
  contract-defined
- undocumented mappings must remain blocked from implementation

This prerequisite/freeze and presence-only alignment exist only to support later safe
adoption of the neutral semantic-fact model and do not change current runtime behavior,
stored payloads, schema surfaces, readiness behavior, or fail-closed behavior.

The canonical `SWE_BODELNING` release eval contract is defined in `schemas/swe-bodelning-release-eval-run.json`, exported through `packages/schemas`, and persisted through the database package.
The canonical `"CMD_PROFILE"` release eval contract is defined in `schemas/cmd-release-eval-run.json`, exported through `packages/schemas`, and mirrors the current canonical release-eval surface for `jurisdiction_profile_key`, release gate/freshness metadata, `evaluator_version`, `release_eval_run_id`, `profile_input_summary`, and `profile_input_lane_snapshot` using the normalized `"cmd_primary_signal"` lane set only. When the runtime dossier seam is enabled, canonical persisted `"CMD_PROFILE"` release eval runs may also carry an attached `profile_dossier_snapshot` derived from the same blocked/current baseline. Runtime support is enabled for `release_eval` in this slice: persistence, governance, and the existing thin read API now support a deterministic blocked/current `"CMD_PROFILE"` release-eval baseline derived only from persisted `"CMD_PROFILE"` profile inputs.
The central governance release-eval adapter/dispatch scaffold is exported from `packages/governance/src/index.js`; it is keyed by `jurisdiction_profile_key`, contains the explicit supported `SWE_BODELNING` adapter entry plus the explicit `"CMD_PROFILE"` adapter entry, and selects canonical release-eval derivation and reconciliation through that registry without changing the current `SWE_BODELNING` output shape.
The explicit `"CMD_PROFILE"` governance release-eval adapter entry is wired only to the documented contract seams already present and derives a deterministic fail-closed blocked baseline from persisted `"CMD_PROFILE"` profile inputs: `release_gate = blocked`, `release_eval_freshness = current`, machine-readable `profile_input_summary`, machine-readable `profile_input_lane_snapshot`, and machine-readable blocked reason codes that distinguish `cmd-input-incomplete` from `cmd-runtime-not-implemented`. Its dossier-related methods now derive deterministic blocked/current dossier snapshot and projection payloads from persisted `"CMD_PROFILE"` release eval data only.
The central packages/schemas release-eval validator dispatch scaffold is exported from `packages/schemas/src/index.js`; it is keyed by `jurisdiction_profile_key`, contains the explicit supported `SWE_BODELNING` validator entry plus the explicit `"CMD_PROFILE"` validator entry, and wires `"CMD_PROFILE"` only to `schemas/cmd-release-eval-run.json` validation through the shared dispatch seam.
The shared blocked/current `release_eval` baseline is explicitly aligned to the neutral stop-outcome contract through `schemas/release-eval-stop-outcome-alignment.json`, exported through `packages/schemas`. That machine-readable alignment covers both `SWE_BODELNING` and `"CMD_PROFILE"` and documents that the current `release_gate = blocked` and `release_eval_freshness = current` baseline maps to canonical `{ "stop_outcome": "blocked" }` while the existing profile-specific `release_gate_reason_code` values remain unchanged.
The shared `release_eval` seam is also explicitly aligned to the neutral stop-matrix contract through `schemas/release-eval-stop-matrix-alignment.json`, exported through `packages/schemas`. This contract-only stop-matrix alignment intentionally covers only the currently concrete `missing_required_input` blocked/current cases already documented and implemented: `swe-bodelning-input-incomplete` for `SWE_BODELNING` and `cmd-input-incomplete` for `"CMD_PROFILE"`. The currently documented `cmd-runtime-not-implemented`, `swe-bodelning-support-incomplete`, and `governance_baseline_fail_closed_pending_completeness_support_policy` release-eval reason codes remain intentionally outside this stop-matrix alignment surface because the current neutral stop-matrix model does not yet define an equivalent principle-level case for them.
The shared `release_eval` seam is also explicitly aligned to the neutral traceability contract through `schemas/release-eval-traceability-alignment.json`, exported through `packages/schemas`. This contract-only traceability alignment intentionally covers only the currently frozen/documented `release_eval` cases that already have explicit input, rule, and canonical output references in the repo contracts: `swe-bodelning-input-incomplete`, `swe-bodelning-support-incomplete`, `cmd-input-incomplete`, and the first documented `"CMD_PROFILE"` rule `cmd-primary-signal-present-but-runtime-not-implemented`. The alignment records canonical `input_references`, `documented_rule_references`, and `canonical_output_references`, and where the current contracts are concrete enough it also records canonical `change_causes` such as `changed_input`, `changed_support`, and `changed_rule`, without changing stored payloads, runtime behavior, or reason codes.

The shared blocked/current `profile_dossier` baseline is explicitly aligned to the neutral stop-outcome contract through `schemas/profile-dossier-stop-outcome-alignment.json`, exported through `packages/schemas`. This contract-only alignment covers the current dossier snapshot/projection baseline semantics for both `SWE_BODELNING` and `"CMD_PROFILE"`: `release_gate = blocked`, `release_eval_freshness = current`, and canonical `{ "stop_outcome": "blocked" }`. The existing profile-specific dossier `release_gate_reason_code` values remain the same canonical reason codes already carried through the shared `release_eval` seam, and dossier `snapshot_status` currentness reporting remains intentionally outside this stop-outcome alignment surface.
The shared `profile_dossier` seam is also explicitly aligned to the neutral stop-matrix contract through `schemas/profile-dossier-stop-matrix-alignment.json`, exported through `packages/schemas`. This contract-only stop-matrix alignment intentionally covers only the currently concrete `missing_required_input` blocked/current dossier cases already documented and inherited from the shared `release_eval` seam: `swe-bodelning-input-incomplete` for `SWE_BODELNING` and `cmd-input-incomplete` for `"CMD_PROFILE"`. The currently documented dossier reason codes `cmd-runtime-not-implemented`, `swe-bodelning-support-incomplete`, and `governance_baseline_fail_closed_pending_completeness_support_policy` remain intentionally outside this dossier stop-matrix alignment surface because the current neutral stop-matrix model does not yet define an equivalent principle-level case for them, and dossier `snapshot_status` currentness reporting remains outside this mapping surface.
The shared `profile_dossier` seam is also explicitly aligned to the neutral traceability contract through `schemas/profile-dossier-traceability-alignment.json`, exported through `packages/schemas`. This contract-only traceability alignment intentionally covers only the currently frozen/documented dossier cases that already have explicit input, rule, and canonical output references in the repo contracts: `swe-bodelning-input-incomplete`, `swe-bodelning-support-incomplete`, `cmd-input-incomplete`, and the first documented `"CMD_PROFILE"` rule `cmd-primary-signal-present-but-runtime-not-implemented` as reflected through the dossier snapshot/projection baseline. The alignment records canonical `input_references`, `documented_rule_references`, and `canonical_output_references`, and where the current contracts are concrete enough it also records canonical `change_causes` such as `changed_input`, `changed_support`, and `changed_rule`, without changing stored payloads, runtime behavior, or reason codes. Dossier `snapshot_status` currentness reporting remains intentionally outside this dossier traceability alignment surface.
